text:
Chandler Stephenson's points look fine: 13 in 19 games, 11 of them assists, six on the power play. The rest of his line is the problem. Seattle gets 38% of the five-on-five shot attempts and expected goals with him on the ice, and the team is more than ten points worse with him than without him. That's the worst relative mark on this list and it isn't close.

This isn't new. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season (-2.0 wins), with opponents getting more chances against him than against almost any forward in the league. In fairness, they also had him playing with some of the weakest teammates anywhere, which drags his raw numbers down.

He's still a two-time Cup winner (Washington in 2018, Vegas in 2023) who skates well and makes plays off the rush: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put 56% of his shots in transition. He hardly shoots himself (16 shots all season). What to watch: whether the Kraken keep feeding him 18 to 22 minutes while the chances against keep piling up, because the assists aren't covering it.
